exhibits.title: The five questions a foreign entrant asks, answered
exhibits.subtitle: Answer, deciding evidence and how sure we are · desk research to early Oct 2026
rows: How big is it, and how fast has it grown?
THB 73 bn data-centre and cloud services in 2025, 24% a year since 2019; ~216 MW of live colocation
THB 20 bn in 2019 [Colliers 2025]; 216 MW live in Q2 2026 [BMI Jun 2026]
Cloud is the bulk of spend; colocation revenue is about a tenth; Bangkok holds two-thirds of live MW
Cloud ~THB 67 bn [AWS TH 2025]; Bangkok 145.8 MW of 216 [BMI Jun 2026]; colocation share [Kira estimates]
What drives it, and the outlook to 2030?
Hyperscale cloud and AI pull; grid access caps the pace; base case ~1.1 GW live by 2030
8.8 GW power-plan allowance [MoE Sep 2026]; scenarios [Kira estimates]
Who leads, and who is gaining?
Thai telcos lead by site count; foreign capital leads the new 100-200 MW builds
NT 13, AIS 8, True IDC 4 of 60 sites [LH Bank 2026]
Where can a foreign company win?
Bangkok AI-ready and interconnection colocation, plus power and cooling supply to the build-out
Segment scoring on the attractiveness pages [Kira estimates]
